research_updates.title: Nine-year electricity series documents operating growth without converting use into cost
research_updates.notes: Apple reports Mesa electricity use rising from 45 million kWh in fiscal 2017 to 563 million kWh in fiscal 2025. The same report says Apple took operational control in October 2015, the converted data center began servicing customers in March 2017, and supporting renewable resources include the 50 MW Bonnybrooke solar project and 4.67 MW of onsite PV. Use is operator-reported rather than utility-meter verified; generation capacity is not load, annual output, avoided cost or capital spending.

research_updates.title: Mesa permit dataset reconciled exhaustively at the address
research_updates.notes: The City of Mesa Socrata endpoint was queried for exact address 3740 S SIGNAL BUTTE RD with a 500-row limit and returned 212 records spanning 2011-2026. Every row was reviewed by permit number, description, issue/final date, status, valuation, invoiced fee, contractor and locality. Thirty-two Apple-era records issued in 2016 or later had a positive valuation and terminal Finaled, C of O Issued or C of C Issued status: eight were already retained and twenty-four omitted records are added here. Their administrative valuations total $209,312,213.34 across separate and sometimes overlapping permits and are deliberately not published as an additive total. Fourteen completed records report $343,013.61 in total invoiced fees, including existing and newly added permits; those fees remain in this audit trail because no global permit-fee metric exists. PMT18-04958 documents two six-inch water meters but reports zero valuation; open, issued-only, fees-due, under-review and revisions-required rows—including BLD2016-07806, BLD2017-00332, BLD2017-03416, PMT26-07994, PMT26-12780 and PMT26-13495—are not treated as completed investment. Pre-Apple manufacturing and transition permits are excluded. Contractor cities identify office addresses only, not contract payment, local ownership, subcontractors, worker residence or local spend.

research_updates.title: Incentive, compliance and audit records do not disclose realized relief
research_updates.notes: Arizona Commerce Authority IOC program reports, the FY2025 annual report, JLBC tax-credit review, Arizona Department of Revenue assessment-ratio material, FTZ Board records and Mesa agreement documents were searched for Apple and the Mesa facility through FY2025. ACA lists Apple as post-approved with a $100 million-plus FY2025 statutory qualifying amount, but expressly says it may include carryover and actual investment is confidential; no new capital record is created. The sources disclose eligibility rules, a prior $25 million state forecast and property classification but no Apple IOC utility-tax relief, transaction-privilege-tax exemption, credit claimed, refund, FTZ duty avoided, grant payment or jurisdiction-level forgone revenue. A forecast midpoint cannot substitute for realization.

research_updates.title: Water and wastewater pathways are direct, quantities remain undisclosed
research_updates.notes: The Apple Mesa AWS certification report, Apple environmental reports for 2018-2026, Mesa water and wastewater planning and rate materials, Greenfield Water Reclamation Plant references, permit records and operator water announcements were reviewed. The AWS audit identifies City of Mesa water supplied from the Signal Butte Water Treatment Plant using CAP/Colorado River water and wastewater sent to Greenfield for treatment, agriculture and recharge. It says the internal water balance and annual variance were quantified, but publishes no values, notes unresolved loss and metering work, and says most effluent is cooling-tower blowdown with domestic sewage below 5%. PMT18-04958 confirms two six-inch meters but no readings or bills. Apple reports implementation of treatment improvements but no Mesa-specific realized savings. Direct annual withdrawal, consumption, discharge, charges and payments remain records-request gaps; electricity-to-WUE conversion is not a substitute.

research_updates.title: County GDP, employment and wage comparisons fail causal prerequisites
research_updates.notes: BLS QCEW downloadable county totals and industry detail, BEA county GDP and earnings, Census County Business Patterns and workforce access were checked for Maricopa County through the latest complete annual vintages. The selected conversion has October 2015 control, 2016 conversion milestones and March 2017 service, while other county data centers and broad regional growth create overlapping treatments. No comparison county, validated parallel trend, facility treatment share, worker-residence bridge or control for simultaneous development was established. Aggregate before-after percentage gaps are descriptive composition changes, not Apple contributions, and all three legacy county-outcome models are removed rather than relabeled as impacts.

assumptions: Class 1 ratio is 16% and the Apple BPP account's observed FTZ ratio is 5%.
Effective tax rates, levies, full cash value and payment behavior remain unchanged.

limitations: No official no-FTZ tax bill is public.
Holds levies and effective tax relations fixed.
Excludes the real-property account and is not a cash grant or net fiscal benefit.

modeled_sources.title: Maricopa County Assessor — Apple Inc. business personal property account 9372704
modeled_sources.notes: The official account names Apple Inc., account 9372704, at 3740 S Signal Butte Road, Mesa. It reports tax-year 2023–2026 full cash value (FCV), FCV assessed value, limited property value (LPV) and LPV assessed value. FCV and LPV, and their assessed amounts, are equal in every displayed year. The account is business personal property and remains separate from the real-property parcel at the same address.

modeled_sources.title: Maricopa County Treasurer — Apple Inc. account 993-72-704
modeled_sources.notes: The official Treasurer account names Apple Inc. and links to assessor business-personal-property account 9372704. Activity records mark tax years 2016–2025 Paid with zero total due. Expanded annual details report assessed tax; the 2025 summary independently reports Full Year and Taxes Paid of $966,899.82. The totals cover all listed taxing districts and are not allocated here to Mesa, Maricopa County, schools or other recipients.

modeled_sources.notes: Reports Class 1 assessment ratios of 17% in 2023, 16.5% in 2024, and 16% in 2025, compared with the 5% Class 6 FTZ ratio.

modeled_scope_note: Foundational accounts re-audited under study-modeling-policy 1.3.0 after renewed direct-evidence searches. Apple Mesa retains three narrowly scoped business-personal-property FTZ counterfactuals from its project fragment; Switch Citadel retains four exact fiscal arithmetic or break-even syntheses; Digital Crossroad Hammond retains two two-account paid-tax arithmetic or break-even syntheses from its project fragment. All other legacy foundational estimates were removed because direct inputs, project scope, time profiles, local allocation, causal identification, or decision relevance were not defensible. Reported observations, forecasts, and remaining models stay separate. Project fragments: prj_study_im3_building_00172739953: Last-resort NAP7 modeling pass under study-modeling-policy-1.3.0. The only retained synthesis is an exact, same-property-account fiscal-year 2027 assessed-liability public-service-cost break-even identity. It uses the directly observed property-tax bill without estimating actual public cost, cash collections, recipient distributions or net fiscal impact. Investment, construction, supplier, operations, resource, community and county outcome candidates were rejected because compatible NAP7 inputs or credible identification are unavailable. prj_study_im3_building_00214321737: Last-resort Markley Lowell model-eligibility pass under study-modeling-policy-1.3.0. The only retained synthesis is an exact same-account FY2026 assessed-liability public-service-cost break-even identity. It uses the directly observed four-quarter real-property bill without estimating actual public cost, cash collections, recipient distributions or net fiscal impact. Investment, construction, supplier, operations, fiscal-net, resource, community and each GDP, employment and wage candidate are rejected separately in the evidence fragment because compatible inputs, scope alignment, non-overlap proof or credible identification are unavailable. prj_study_im3_building_00300974499: Corrective policy-1.3.0 synthesis. Three legacy combined real-and-personal-property FTZ counterfactuals are superseded by narrower business-personal-property-only estimates because the Apple BPP account directly exhibits the 5% assessment ratio while the real-property account has a different valuation base. The replacements hold observed effective tax rates and full cash value constant and isolate only the assessment-ratio component; they are not cash grants, audited forgone-revenue amounts or net fiscal benefits. All other legacy Apple Mesa estimates fail the direct-evidence, scope, time-profile, geography or decision-relevance gates and are marked for removal in the evidence fragment. prj_study_im3_building_00364289074: Corrective residual modeled account for Microsoft San Antonio. Eight transferred construction, labor, procurement, operating, and household-output scenarios were removed because their arbitrary capital shares, forecast-realization cases, local-purchase assumptions, and Virginia coefficients were not bounded by project observations. Only three low-confidence descriptive county comparisons remain: each uses the project's documented operating-by 2013 anchor and official Bexar County outcome data, has a finite fit-sensitivity envelope, and explicitly makes no causal attribution. The account intentionally remains incomplete because no defensible direct observation or residual model closes the supplier category. prj_study_im3_building_00377585075: Corrective DET01 synthesis. Only exact same-period tax-account arithmetic, its explicitly conditional public-cost break-even identity and a unit conversion of displayed municipal meter history remain. Construction, employment, supplier, household, electricity, cooling, emissions, wastewater and county-effect models were removed because the audit did not bound the missing project inputs. This account is intentionally incomplete where direct evidence remains unbounded. prj_study_im3_building_00460089167: Corrective audit retains six bounded residual calculations only: FY2025 county tax retained after the provisionally linked incentive, the identical marginal-service-cost break-even threshold, conversion of Meta-reported 2024 water withdrawal with source rounding, and three noncausal county comparison gaps with fit sensitivity. Ten models based on arbitrary capital timing, cost shares, FTE ratios, transferred operating/construction multipliers, fleet PUE, or wastewater ratios are removed. Supplier/local-procurement evidence remains unavailable, so the project is intentionally incomplete rather than backfilled. prj_study_im3_building_00464097467: Second-pass modeled contribution account after an expanded public-evidence audit. Direct county permits now cover historical construction values, assessor rolls cover a main-campus parcel stock, a county action covers water-right capacity, Apple reports 2025 campus electricity use, and recipient reports bound two community gifts. Those observations supersede the need for a modeled community proxy but do not supply Apple contractor job-years, construction payroll, annual operating payroll, supplier payments, taxes received, or public-service cost. The construction base therefore retains only the packet's explicit $163 million construction forecast and excludes equipment and historical capital; wide 0.5-1.5 transfer sensitivities expose the mismatch in the last-resort direct construction coefficients. The unsupported local-purchase-share and Virginia induced-output models are removed. No net-fiscal value or public-service-cost break-even is published. County outcome gaps remain descriptive benchmark applications with fit-sensitivity intervals and no causal-design metadata. prj_study_im3_building_00598261190: Dedicated last-resort model-eligibility pass for State Farm Olathe under study-modeling-policy-1.3.0. Four bounded syntheses are retained: the exact 2025 parcel-tax-payment identity as a same-account public-service-cost break-even threshold, plus low-confidence descriptive 2024 Johnson County GDP, employment and wage comparison gaps using the repository's pre-2016 inverse-distance benchmark. No estimate is an observed cost, net fiscal result or causal facility effect. Supplier/local-spend and community-allocation candidates, an HPIP credit counterfactual, and causal county designs are rejected because the project-specific inputs, scope matches, non-overlap proof or identification conditions recorded in the evidence fragment are absent. prj_study_im3_building_00664938835: Second-pass Expedient Milwaukee / Franklin syntheses retained only after a documented 2007-2026 public-source audit. The account keeps a clearly labeled 2022 ownership-transfer anchor, a PB25-0303-only construction allocation sensitivity, an exact tax-equal public-cost break-even threshold, a capacity-based electricity engineering sensitivity, and three descriptive county comparison gaps. It removes transferred construction job-years, assumed local-purchase shares, supplier and household output extrapolations, and a duplicate modeled tax row because public sources did not establish realized site employment, supplier geography, household capture, or a need to restate the direct tax observations. PM25-0174 remains excluded for possible overlap. No synthesis is an observed result or fiscal net. prj_study_im3_building_00844389014: Second-pass model review retains one bounded resource identity only. It reproduces Google-reported 2024 Montgomery County water consumption as withdrawal minus discharge after converting displayed million-gallon values to gallons, with a rounding envelope. Direct searches of Clarksville utility/public-works pages, county stormwater records, TDEC/EPA portals and CDE/TVA materials did not surface a building meter, utility bill or a compatible canonical observed-water metric. The amount remains unallocated across the location and inventory buildings; discharge may be engineering-estimated. No transferred multiplier, supplier-retention assumption, energy proxy, fiscal result, public-cost threshold, payroll estimate or causal county outcome is modeled. prj_study_im3_building_00888253616: Residual synthesis after the SV1 public-source audit. It retains one exact tax-equal public-cost break-even threshold and three reproducible but low-confidence county comparison gaps. The county gaps use 2013-2020 pre-opening histories and an inverse-distance-weighted 20-county benchmark; very wide fit envelopes are retained because Santa Clara County matches poorly. No model converts capacity to consumption, permit value to jobs, or unidentified vendor and community activity to local benefits. prj_study_im3_building_00978934687: Corrective residual synthesis for Digital Crossroad DX-1 under study-modeling-policy-1.3.0. Of 43 legacy estimates, none is retained unchanged: 41 are directed for removal and two are revised using the complete 2024-pay-2025 paid-tax base for the leasehold real account and DX Hammond JV LLC personal-property account. The revised contribution is an exact account-level aggregation across local taxing authorities, and the companion public-service-cost estimate is only the equal-cost break-even identity; neither is an audited recipient receipt, observed public cost or net fiscal result. New estimate IDs prevent silent mutation of the legacy base and their notes identify the superseded estimates for orchestrator reconciliation. prj_study_im3_building_01073720208: Second-pass governed synthesis for Google Council Bluffs. Construction job-years use only two directly observed September 2025 city permit valuations and transfer the published Prince William County prototype coefficients as benchmark equivalents; the four channels are separated and protected by one aggregation. No Pottawattamie County supplier-retention share is imposed because the public audit found contractor names but no payment or vendor-residence ledger. The water row is the unallocated Google Council Bluffs location identity reported for 2024, not a building allocation. No local abatement, exemption realization, franchise-fee amount, electric load, public-service cost, break-even threshold, or net fiscal result is modeled. County outcome gaps remain descriptive benchmark applications with fit-sensitivity ranges and no causal attribution. prj_study_im3_building_01132541700: Four bounded syntheses are retained after direct-record search: one deterministic conversion of Meta's rounded 2024 Henrico water-withdrawal observation and three governed, descriptive county comparison gaps. No construction, operating, supplier, household, tax-receipt, incentive-cost, or public-service-cost model is added because the public record lacks the needed project-specific bases and arbitrary allocation shares would create false precision. Every retained estimate is visibly modeled, unallocated to the selected building, non-additive, and noncausal. prj_study_im3_campus_00019988712: Residual synthesis after the Meta Prineville direct-evidence audit. One medium-confidence unit conversion carries Meta's rounded 2024 facility-level water-withdrawal observation from megaliters to gallons because the shared direct register has no compatible annual-withdrawal metric. The three low-confidence county benchmark comparisons were removed: even with fit-sensitivity envelopes and explicit non-causal labels, they do not materially improve decisions about this campus and remain vulnerable to concurrent Meta expansions, Apple's separate campus and unrelated county changes. No supplier, construction, payroll, household-spending, tax-abatement, public-service-cost or fiscal-net model is retained because local inputs and same-scope evidence are insufficient. prj_study_im3_campus_00231769626: Residual synthesis after the Google The Dalles public-source audit. Only three low-confidence descriptive county comparison gaps are retained because the direct record does not identify causal county outcomes. Each benchmark uses the available 2001-2005 pre-opening history, excludes all study counties from a 20-county inverse-distance-weighted donor pool, and carries a fit-sensitivity envelope. No model converts broad investment or permit values to jobs, onsite contractor counts to supplier output, utility-system loads to campus consumption, tax bills to payments, or unmatched incentive formulas and public costs to a fiscal net. prj_study_im3_campus_00675108684: Dedicated last-resort Boydton model-eligibility pass under study-modeling-policy-1.3.0. Retained syntheses are limited to exact arithmetic over cited compatible observations: a five-fiscal-year average of the operator-reported portfolio property-tax total, its explicitly conditional same-scope public-cost break-even identity, and annual sums of identified LVL/Herbert Fund 301 components. All remain unallocated, modeled rather than observed, and non-additive to their source totals. COF phase investment, operating headcount, construction, resources, suppliers, induced effects, causal comparisons and net fiscal impact were rejected because overlap, timing, scope or required project inputs remain unresolved.
legacy_first_entry_note: Two exact Maricopa County facilities are documented operational before Apple's March 2017 service date. The Apple event is therefore rejected as the county's first operational entry. The broader 55-facility historical inventory has not been proven complete, so the county's true first entry remains unresolved and no treatment date is assigned.

project_description: Apple Mesa is a converted and expanded data-center facility at 3740 South Signal Butte Road in Mesa, Arizona. Apple took operational control in October 2015, and the site began serving customers in March 2017; the account keeps the real-estate parcel, Apple-owned equipment, later data-hall permits, renewable-energy support, and facility electricity reporting distinct.
